- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. - general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

input.prompt:
I need to trace the complete call chain for creating a memo in this project, from the frontend React mutation hook down to the SQL INSERT statement. Search very thoroughly for each of these layers:

1. Frontend mutation hook - look for something like useCreateMemo, useMemoStore, or a mutation hook that calls a create memo RPC. Check in web/src/ or frontend directories.
2. Client/service layer - the gRPC or API client that sends the create memo request. Look in proto/ or api/ directories.
3. Proto RPC definition - the .proto file defining the CreateMemo RPC.
4. Server handler/service - the Go handler that implements the CreateMemo RPC. Look in server/ or internal/ directories.
5. Store method - the Go store/repository method that does the actual database insert. Look in store/ directory.
6. Dialect driver - the specific SQL dialect driver (e.g., postgres, mysql, sqlite) that has the INSERT SQL statement for memos.

For each layer, give me the exact file path. Search breadth: very thorough.

I now have all the information needed. Here is the complete call chain for creating a memo, from frontend to SQL.

---

## Complete Create Memo Call Chain

### Layer 1 -- Frontend Editor Save Hook (entry point)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoEditor/hooks/useMemoSave.ts`

The `useMemoSave` hook (line 28) is the top-level entry point triggered by the editor toolbar or keyboard shortcut. On save, it calls `memoService.save(state, { memoName, parentMemoName })` at line 53.

### Layer 2 -- Frontend Service Layer (builds the RPC request)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/components/MemoEditor/services/memoService.ts`

The `memoService.save()` method (line 77) handles the branching logic:
- For **new memos** (no existing `memoName`), it calls `memoServiceClient.createMemo({ memo: memoData })` at line 120.
- For **comments**, it calls `memoServiceClient.createMemoComment(...)` at line 116.
- For **updates** to existing memos, it calls `memoServiceClient.updateMemo(...)` at line 97.

There is also a standalone React Query mutation hook:

**File:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/hooks/useMemoQueries.ts`

The `useCreateMemo()` hook (line 178) wraps `memoServiceClient.createMemo({ memo: memoToCreate })` in a `useMutation` with cache invalidation on success.

### Layer 3 -- gRPC/Connect Client (transport)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/web/src/connect.ts`

`memoServiceClient` is created at line 197:
```ts
export const memoServiceClient = createClient(MemoService, transport);
```
The `transport` is a Connect-Web transport (line 184) using binary protobuf format, with an auth interceptor that attaches Bearer tokens and handles 401 refresh/retry. The `MemoService` descriptor is imported from the generated protobuf TypeScript bindings.

### Layer 4 -- Proto RPC Definition

**File:** `/bench/home/work/proto/api/v1/memo_service.proto`

The `CreateMemo` RPC is defined at lines 21-27:
```proto
rpc CreateMemo(CreateMemoRequest) returns (Memo) {
    option (google.api.http) = {
      post: "/api/v1/memos"
      body: "memo"
    };
    option (google.api.method_signature) = "memo";
  }
```
The `CreateMemoRequest` message is defined at lines 293-300, containing a required `Memo memo` field and an optional `string memo_id`.

### Layer 5 -- Server Handler (Go gRPC implementation)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go`

The `CreateMemo` method starts at line 70:
```go
func (s *APIV1Service) CreateMemo(ctx context.Context, request *v1pb.CreateMemoRequest) (*v1pb.Memo, error) {
```
It:
1. Authenticates the user (line 71)
2. Validates/generates a UID (line 79)
3. Builds a `store.Memo` struct with UID, CreatorID, Content, Visibility (lines 84-89)
4. Optionally sets custom timestamps (lines 92-99)
5. Enforces the content length limit (lines 101-107)
6. Rebuilds the memo payload (line 108)
7. Calls `s.Store.CreateMemo(ctx, create)` at line 115
8. Handles attachments and relations (lines 127-146)
9. Dispatches webhook and SSE events (lines 157-168)

### Layer 6 -- Store Method (domain/repository layer)

**File:** `/bench/home/work/store/memo.go`

The `Store.CreateMemo` method at line 109 validates the UID and delegates to the database driver:
```go
func (s *Store) CreateMemo(ctx context.Context, create *Memo) (*Memo, error) {
    if !base.UIDMatcher.MatchString(create.UID) {
        return nil, errors.New("invalid uid")
    }
    return s.driver.CreateMemo(ctx, create)
}
```

The `Driver` interface is defined in:

**File:** `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go`

At line 29: `CreateMemo(ctx context.Context, create *Memo) (*Memo, error)`

### Layer 7 -- SQL Dialect Drivers (actual INSERT statements)

Three dialect implementations exist:

**PostgreSQL:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/memo.go`
- `CreateMemo` at line 16
- SQL (line 38): `INSERT INTO memo (uid, creator_id, content, visibility, payload [, created_ts] [, updated_ts]) VALUES ($1, $2, ...) RETURNING id, created_ts, updated_ts, row_status`
- Uses numbered `$N` placeholders; optional timestamp columns are appended dynamically.

**SQLite:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/memo.go`
- `CreateMemo` at line 16
- SQL (line 41): ``INSERT INTO `memo` (`uid`, `creator_id`, `content`, `visibility`, `payload` [, `created_ts`] [, `updated_ts`]) VALUES (?, ?, ...) RETURNING `id`, `created_ts`, `updated_ts`, `row_status` ``
- Uses `?` placeholders with backtick-quoted identifiers.

**MySQL:** `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/memo.go`
- `CreateMemo` at line 16
- SQL (line 41): ``INSERT INTO `memo` (`uid`, `creator_id`, `content`, `visibility`, `payload` [, `created_ts`] [, `updated_ts`]) VALUES (?, ?, ..., FROM_UNIXTIME(?))``
- Uses `FROM_UNIXTIME(?)` for timestamp columns. Does not use `RETURNING`; instead calls `result.LastInsertId()` and then re-fetches the full row with `GetMemo`.

---

### Summary of the call chain

```
useMemoSave (hooks/useMemoSave.ts:53)
  -> memoService.save (services/memoService.ts:120)
    -> memoServiceClient.createMemo (connect.ts:197, via Connect-Web transport)
      -> HTTP POST /api/v1/memos (proto: memo_service.proto:21, CreateMemoRequest at line 293)
        -> APIV1Service.CreateMemo (server memo_service.go:70)
          -> Store.CreateMemo (store/memo.go:109)
            -> Driver.CreateMemo (store/driver.go:29)
              -> postgres/memo.go:16  -- INSERT INTO memo (...) VALUES (...) RETURNING ...
              -> sqlite/memo.go:16   -- INSERT INTO `memo` (...) VALUES (...) RETURNING ...
              -> mysql/memo.go:16    -- INSERT INTO `memo` (...) VALUES (...)
```
